headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: OpenHands can ingest mounted files and broad-egress MCP actions while Haystack can route content through MCP/REST without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP. That creates a plausible shared-channel bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests content from an MCP server or REST source that OpenHands can influence, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenHands mounts a shared workspace that Haystack also reads, file-based instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Separate their workspaces so no file bridge exists.
Require provenance tagging on all retrieved content.
Add a manual review step before either agent acts on external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands explicitly reads files in its runtime sandbox and has broad network egress; Haystack also has broad network egress and can call MCP/REST APIs. Even though Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, the pair can still move mounted file contents or runtime context across network boundaries in default setups. The shared-data path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF OpenHands is given mounted files containing sensitive material, those contents can be exposed through its networked actions.
IF Haystack is connected to external APIs or MCP servers that receive retrieved content, that content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive files into OpenHands.
Restrict Haystack to approved local-only backends.
Block outbound network access except to allowlisted endpoints.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Review logs for accidental content transmission.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem and modify_git_state plus shell/subprocess execution, while Haystack can also interact with files via MCP/REST workflows and broad egress. If both are pointed at the same repository or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The profiles do not show coordination primitives, so the conflict risk is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory or git checkout, write conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are allowed to modify git state without an external lock, history corruption or lost updates are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Disable one agent's write access during the other's run.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Run a quick diff check before merging outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent that can surface retrieved content, and OpenHands is an action-taking coding agent with shell, browser, and filesystem write authority. If OpenHands treats Haystack output as authoritative, a bad retrieval or hallucinated fact can cascade into code changes, commits, or external actions. No verification step is documented in the pair, so the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Haystack output without independent verification, erroneous facts can drive actions.
IF Haystack retrieves stale or malicious content and OpenHands commits based on it, downstream damage can persist.
mitigations: Require source links for every factual claim.
Add a human approval gate before commits or external actions.
Compare Haystack output against a second source.
Limit OpenHands to dry-run mode for the first pass.
Log and diff all agent-generated changes.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, while OpenHands handles files in its runtime and model provider API keys. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is visible: OpenHands may process mounted files under broader retention/logging than Haystack. Because the other agent is not clearly implicated in a specific regulated-data flow, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into OpenHands, its runtime handling may create retention or logging obligations.
IF Haystack is later connected to regulated datasets, the pair may need policy alignment.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings before each run.
Use separate storage buckets for each agent.
Document data-class handling in the runbook.
